name: Weaviate B.V.
origin_detail: Open-source project on GitHub since March 2016 (BSD-3-Clause from April 2016); company founded in 2019 in Amsterdam by Bob van Luijt (CEO) and Etienne Dilocker, first as SeMI Technologies B.V. and renamed Weaviate B.V. (LICENSE updated Jan 2023); remote-first with offices in the US and Australia
openness_notes: Initial 3: from April 2016 to August 2026 the entire repository was BSD-3-Clause and revenue came from Weaviate Cloud and support. Current 2 (open core): on 2026-08-26 Weaviate added a proprietary 'Weaviate License' (copyright Weaviate BV, all rights reserved, enterprise licence required) for code under the repo's wl/ directory, enabled by a licence key; BSD-3 still covers everything else, and the Community Edition remains free with no time limits or usage caps. Between Sep and Nov 2026 existing features were moved into wl/ and gated (namespaces, shard self-recovery, deduplicated backups, DB-user expiry, the rebalance planner). The source stays visible on GitHub but is not OSI-licensed.

license_history.license: BSD-3-Clause outside wl/; proprietary Weaviate License (enterprise, licence key) for wl/
license_history.note: Added 2026-08-26 (commit 8677d32); text replaced 'per legal' 2026-09-30 (e0cc80c); licence key LICENSE_KEY/LICENSE_KEY_FILE since 2026-09-15

relicensing_events.to: BSD-3-Clause core + proprietary Weaviate License for enterprise features in wl/
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Partial closing, GitLab-style open core rather than an SSPL/BSL relicense of the whole database: existing code was moved into wl/ and gated (namespaces 2026-09-28, self-recovery orchestrator 2026-09-29, deduplicated backups 2026-09-30/10-01, rebalance planner 2026-11-23 'to gate behind enterprise'). Earlier releases remain BSD-3; no fork found as of 2026-11-24.

risk_events: Aug-Nov 2026: shift to open core; existing features moved behind a licence key in a proprietary wl/ directory
Oct 2026: GraphQL API deprecation announced (2026-10-22), a breaking change for existing users
Sep-Oct 2026: security releases, including a high-severity fix for Google modules (2026-09-17)
robustness: The BSD-3 core and all pre-August-2026 releases remain forkable, and the project has 16,958 GitHub stars (Nov 2026) and 2M+ downloads (Apr 2023), but governance is single-vendor with a contributor licence agreement, and new operational features now land in the proprietary wl/ directory.
physical_science_relevance: General retrieval infrastructure (vector and hybrid search for RAG and agents); no science-specific deployments were confirmed on fetched pages.
openness_effect_assessment: A permissive BSD-3 database gave Weaviate early adoption (2M+ downloads by the Apr 2023 Series B) and investor interest ($50M led by Index Ventures). Seven years after incorporation, alongside its Weaviate Cloud service, it moved to open core in 2026, gating operational features for self-managed deployments behind an enterprise licence rather than relicensing the database itself; the effect on community or revenue is not yet observable.
key_takeaway: Weaviate shows the AI-era version of the database 'closing' pattern in a milder form: instead of an SSPL- or BSL-style relicense of the whole product (MongoDB, Elastic, HashiCorp), it kept the core BSD-3 and in Aug-Nov 2026 carved out a proprietary enterprise directory, moving existing features into it. Permissive licensing helped it grow; monetizing self-hosted users still pushed it toward open core.

The wl/ directory holds backupdedupe, dbusers, namespaces, rebalance and selfrecovery. Some of these features may have been developed in 2026 rather than previously released under BSD-3; commit messages show at least namespacing prefixing, the self-recovery orchestrator, dedupe backup planning and the RebalancePlanner were moved there from elsewhere in the repo.
GitHub API reports licence NOASSERTION because of the dual LICENSE structure.
Commits adding the licence switch (2026-08-26) carry a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' trailer; noted only as provenance.
